Performers
Philadelphia Orchestra (orchestra), Leopold Stokowski (conductor), Thaddeus Rich (solo violin) Documented

The Discography of American Historical Recordings, from the disc labels, names the Philadelphia Orchestra and Stokowski. The solo violinist is credited only in the transferor’s description of the Internet Archive item, which names Thaddeus Rich; the labels as transcribed by DAHR do not.

[3] [4] [1]
Work version
Symphonic poem for orchestra with solo violin, 1874; the whole work on two disc sides joined into one file Documented

The transferor says the file joins the two sides of Victor 6505. The score edition and any cuts are not established from the sources.

[1] [3] [4] [7]
Recorded
1925-04-29 Documented

Take date of the issued takes (take 2 of each side). DAHR also lists an earlier take 1 of each side under matrices C-27929 and C-27930.

[3] [4]
Place
Camden, New Jersey Documented

Victor’s Camden studios; the DAHR entry names the city only.

[3] [4]
Label
Victor Documented

DAHR lists later issues of the same takes as Victor 6653/6654 and 01527/01528, and Gramophone (HMV) DB 961 and others.

[3] [4] [5]
Catalogue
Victor 6505 Documented

Twelve-inch double-sided Red Seal disc, Part 1 on one side and Part 2 on the other. Victor’s supplement of 1 December 1925 lists Danse Macabre by the Philadelphia Orchestra as 6505, 12-inch, $2.00.

[3] [4] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
CVE-27929 (Part 1) and CVE-27930 (Part 2), take 2 of each Documented

Matrix numbers and takes come from DAHR. Take 3 of each was destroyed. No runout inscription has been inspected.

[3] [4]
Transfer
Bob Varney Documented

The Internet Archive item (added 16 September 2010) says “Transfer by Bob Varney from Victor 6505 issued in 1925”.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Archive’s date of addition is not a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

Equalisation, speed correction and noise reduction are not described. In this file the opening harp strokes sit close to concert pitch. A later Internet Archive transfer of the same sides (Philadelphia Symphony Orchestra – Danse Macabre, 2012, which is also the Wikimedia Commons file) runs about 2% faster and roughly a third of a semitone sharper, which is why this transfer is the one used.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Public domain: Saint-⁠Saëns died on 16 December 1921 Documented

More than seventy years after the composer’s death; the underlying work is free of copyright in the EU and the US.

[8]
Recording rights
Public domain in the United States: first published in 1925 on Victor 6505; this transfer carries a CC BY 3.0 licence from its maker Documented

Victor’s catalogue supplement of 1 December 1925 already lists 6505 among the records issued since the last edition of its catalogue, so first publication falls in 1925 or earlier. US sound recordings published before 1 January 1926 are public domain under 17 U.S.C. § 1401 (Wikimedia Commons template PD-US-record-expired). Publication in 1925 also falls before the project’s 1963 cut-off for the EU phonogram term. The Internet Archive item’s licence field names CC BY 3.0, which applies to Bob Varney’s transfer.
